No. The 2025 loss is a **candidate, pending corroboration**, and its persistence has not been established.

Hansen/UMD mapped approximately 13.5 ha of tree-cover loss in 2025, or 3.91% of the asset. The JRC 2020 forest map agrees with 98% of the event area, but 2025 is the latest observed year. A later year is needed to assess persistence and meet the corroboration rule.

The evidence also does not establish the cause of the loss or whether it involved deforestation or land-use change.
